brief.t: Desk projection **21.0 m 480-lb bales** (269 lakh Indian bales) for 2026-27, range 19.7–22.3, vs USDA 24.0 and 22.6 last season (-7%). Area is about flat (-0.6%), so the cut is yield: Maharashtra -13% (Aug–Sep rain -63%), Gujarat -7% (Aug–Sep rain -34%), Telangana + AP -9% (Aug–Sep rain -38%), Karnataka -9% (Aug–Sep rain -34%).

June–September rain across the cotton areas was -19% vs the 1991-2020 normal, the 5th driest of 36 years (drier only in 1999, 2000, 2001, 2002). Maharashtra, a third of India's cotton area, had -30%, the driest since at least 1991, with August–September -63% when bolls fill. October has been dry as well, which helps picking but not yield.

For 2025-26 the official COCPC sheet ends with 3.3 m bales of stock and the trade's CAI sheet (2026-07) with 7.3 m; they differ mainly on the crop (22.7 vs 26.5 m). A crop near the desk number would pull 2026-27 stocks down from either level.
Raw cotton imports 2025-2026 through 2026-08: 1.14 mt (5.2 m bales), +74% on the same months of 2024-2025; exports 324 kt (-17%). India has turned into a steady importer.

Shankar-6 ₹66,700/candy = 89.4¢/lb (2026-10-29), +10.9¢ over ICE nearby and +26% on a year ago; the MSP floor works out to about 86¢/lb lint, so CCI support sits just under the market. Indian cotton is dear against the world.

Customs data show 2025-26 imports of 63.5 lakh bales through 2026-08 (about 69 for the season at the recent pace) vs 55 in the official COCPC sheet, so last season's closing stock is nearer 55 lakh than 43. With the desk crop, imports and exports at the customs pace and use held at last season's level, 2026-27 ends with **3.3 m 480-lb bales** (42 lakh; stocks/use 12% vs 16%). Holding last season's stocks/use would take about 6.4 m bales of imports (82 lakh), against USDA's 3.3 m.

Customs data show imports run at about 0.44 m bales a month duty-free and 0.22 m with the 11% duty, with a rush before each deadline (December 2025 was double the months before, then imports fell to 0.08 m in February). Keeping USDA's 2025-26 and its 2026-27 use (26.5 m), with the desk crop (21.0 m): if the duty returns in November as notified, imports are **3.3 m** (about USDA's 3.3 m, so that is the floor) and ending stocks 7.8 m; duty-free to December as expected, **4.5 m** and 8.9 m; duty-free all season, **5.3 m** and 9.8 m (USDA 10.4 m). So imports rise a lot only if the waiver runs well past December; each extra duty-free month adds roughly 0.22 m.

Over the last 12 months of origin data (2025-08 to 2026-07) India's imports came 30% from Brazil, 28% Africa, 20% Australia and 17% from the US. Timing decides the US share: in the Sep–Dec 2025 duty-free window the US got only 14% (Brazil, Australia and Africa have new crop then), in the Apr–Oct 2022 window 35% (US shipping season, Brazil out of cotton). With each origin's 2026/27 exportable supply (Australia -26%, the US -7% on the desk crop), US cotton to India is about 0.8 m bales if the duty returns in November, **0.9 m** with the waiver to December (+0.16 m; Brazil +0.46, Africa +0.32) and 1.5 m if it runs all season (+0.71 m, most of it March–July). US commitments to India are 0.28 m (week of 2026-10-22), so new US sales still to come are about 0.5 m, **0.7 m** and **1.2 m** in the three cases.

The Cotton Corporation of India bought 104 lakh bales of the 2025-26 crop at MSP and had sold 92 lakh by 2026-08-14, leaving about 12 lakh (0.9 m bales); at its recent pace of about 1.9 lakh a week the reserve is close to empty, so carry-in stocks sit with mills and traders, not the government. New-crop buying at the 8,267 rupee MSP started in October; with Shankar-6 above the MSP-implied lint cost, CCI should buy less than last season unless prices fall.

A smaller Indian crop, duty-free imports (waiver expected through December) and Indian prices well above ICE all point to more Indian import demand in 2026-27 than USDA's number, with US and Brazilian cotton the main suppliers.
